extracted.intended_audience: librarians, informationists, and researchers wanting training in conducting or supporting systematic reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Learning objectives for a mixed online/in-person workshop teaching foundations, search and data-management methods, librarian roles, and strategies to establish expertise in systematic reviews at one's institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid foundation of the systematic review process
rubrics_metrics.description: With its mix of online and in-person instruction, you should expect to leave the workshop with a solid foundation of the systematic review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course framing indicates foundational coverage of the overall process (scoping, protocol, searching, screening, data extraction, synthesis) though specific sub-steps are addressed in later items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective methods for conducting and communicating about systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave the workshop with effective methods for conducting and communicating about systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practical approaches for both executing reviews and communicating methods/results to stakeholders; implies emphasis on reproducibility and clear reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete strategies to demonstrate your expertise at your institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave the workshop with concrete strategies to demonstrate your expertise at your institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance and an opportunity to develop an action plan to establish oneself as a recognized resource for systematic review expertise locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: The basics of a systematic review — study types and methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: The basics of a systematic review — study types and methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces different review types and appropriate methodological choices for each (e.g., randomized trials vs observational evidence) — foundational conceptual knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Librarian roles on systematic review teams
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: Librarian roles on systematic review teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains typical and recommended contributions of librarians/informationists (e.g., protocol development, search design, documentation, reporting) and how to participate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting databases and developing search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: Selecting databases and developing search strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instruction on choosing appropriate bibliographic resources and constructing searches tailored to review questions; links to techniques for thorough and replicable searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grey literature resources and considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: Grey literature resources and considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers identification and use of non‑published or hard-to-find sources (clinical trial registries, conference proceedings, theses) and the considerations for inclusion and searching of grey literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management, documentation, and writing for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: Data management, documentation, and writing for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction on organizing review data, keeping reproducible documentation of searches and decisions, and best practices for preparing manuscripts and reporting results for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies to establish your presence and expertise at your home institution
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will cover: Strategies to establish your presence and expertise at your home institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on outreach, service models, and demonstrating value to researchers and administrators; ties to the workshop's action-plan exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify resources for published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of the course, you should be able to identify: Resources for published literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners are expected to recognize which databases and indexes cover relevant published studies for a given review topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify resources for grey literature and unpublished studies
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of the course, you should be able to identify: Resources for grey literature and unpublished studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners should be able to locate trial registries, institutional repositories, conference materials, and other sources of unpublished or grey evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques for constructing thorough and replicable searches
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of the course, you should be able to identify: Techniques for constructing thorough and replicable searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on reproducibility: documenting search strings, using appropriate controlled vocabulary and keywords, peer-review of search strategies, and adapting searches across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques for data management and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of the course, you should be able to identify: Techniques for data management and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers methods for organizing extracted data, version control of documentation, tracking screening and extraction decisions, and standards for reporting (PRISMA-style elements implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits and barriers to librarian participation on a systematic review team
rubrics_metrics.description: By the end of the course, you should be able to identify: Benefits and barriers to librarian participation on a systematic review team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps learners weigh institutional, workload, and recognition factors that enable or hinder meaningful librarian involvement and plan strategies to address barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an action plan to establish yourself as a recognized resource
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll also have the opportunity to develop an action plan to establish yourself as a recognized resource for systematic review expertise at your home institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on exercise to translate workshop learnings into concrete steps (e.g., outreach, service offerings, documentation templates) to increase visibility and uptake of librarian services.
